title: Spectral Analysis Workstation
description: A chemistry lab workstation where a barn lamp serves as a UV/visible-light emission source for spectral analysis. The user must don protective Khronos sunglasses, calibrate the lamp through multiple wavelength bands, position a virtual sample, and record absorption readings across the spectrum to identify an unknown compound.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive spectral analysis chemistry lab. Load AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb as the primary light emission source mounted on a lab bench, and SunglassesKhronos.glb as protective lab eyewear resting on the bench nearby. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.6, 3) looking at the bench, with OrbitControls limited to a 90-degree arc. Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and a directional light simulating overhead fluorescents. The interaction sequence has 8 validated steps: (1) Click the sunglasses to pick them up — they animate toward the camera and attach to the view with slight transparency overlay tint, enabling a UV-filter HUD. (2) Click the barn lamp to power it on — its emissive materials glow and a visible PointLight activates at its bulb position. (3) Use a wavelength slider (380nm–780nm) in an HTML overlay panel to set the lamp emission band — the PointLight color must update to the correct visible spectrum color using wavelength-to-RGB conversion. (4) Click a 'Place Sample' button to spawn a translucent cylinder (the cuvette) between the lamp and a detector plane. (5) Adjust a concentration slider (0.1–2.0 mol/L) that changes the cuvette opacity accordingly. (6) Click 'Record Reading' to capture the current transmittance value (calculated from concentration and wavelength using a simplified Beer-Lambert formula A=εcl) and plot it on a canvas-based chart in the HUD. (7) Repeat steps 3 and 6 at least three different wavelengths — validate that at least 3 distinct readings exist. (8) Click 'Identify Compound' which compares the absorption curve peak to a predefined table and displays the compound name. Validate each step sequentially with a status bar showing progress. The sunglasses HUD overlay should tint the renderer output with a slight amber tone using a CSS filter. All parameter values must be clamped and validated before proceeding.
